6.37.3 What the executed capacity result establishes
The retained 382,396-byte request becomes 175,016 bytes under this encoding, leaving
24,984 bytes below the unchanged limit. Decoding reproduces the original request ex-
actly. All 263 source units and all 263 concerns survive. An offline integration run then
processes the same full source, recreates the same coverage records, and completes the
final reconciliation using a synthetic response provider. Its final dispositions retain
all concerns as unresolved. This exercise demonstrates that the whole-context control
flow can finish within the byte bound; it supplies no legal answer to the authentication
circular.
The first integration diagnostic also exposed an instructive harness mistake. Its syn-
thetic respondent described an unencoded reading as an executable proposal. The
validator rejected that response. The repair changed the synthetic response to retain
uncertainty, preserving both the failed diagnostic and the rejection rule. Changing the
rule to make the exercise succeed would have concealed the same error that the inter-
pretation procedures are intended to detect.
A second capacity challenge gives each unit a long, unique rationale and each concern
additional evidence. Its exact representation exceeds the same limit. The system re-
tains that request and its successful round-trip check, then stops before provider dis-
patch. This outcome is necessary: an encoding cannot promise to fit an arbitrarily large
collection of different explanations into a fixed request. A future source that reaches
this limit needs a separately justified capacity or reasoning strategy. Dropping qualifi-
cations would change the question being investigated.
The new encoding is an explicit optional protocol, readable-tables.v1.
Existing
recorded routes retain their identities; a changed encoding cannot reuse a journal
as though its request protocol were unchanged. No live model call was used in this
capacity exercise, and the exhausted original allowance and issue histories remain
intact.
Model comprehension of this representation is untested.
The subsequent
executable quotation and date-proof extensions are described in Section 6.38. Unre-
solved incorporated sources and an observed prospective evaluation window remain
open. The flow chart on page xxiv connects the preservation check to those continuing
uncertainties.
6.38 Checking executable quotations and calendar
comparisons
The processing repairs leave two precise engineering questions. Can an interpretation
proposal point to the exact executable expression it discusses? Can the date compar-
isons in the retained UCITS proposals receive a formal preservation check? Both ques-
tions can be addressed without making a model’s legal judgment an answer key. They
require different evidence: one concerns the identity of a quotation, the other a declared
mathematical meaning.

Chapter 6
6.38.1 A quotation must identify the actual expression
A source quotation and a program quotation have different subjects. The first identifies
words in a circular. The second identifies the expression proposed to implement a read-
ing of those words. A model may quote the right circular while describing a formula
that was never encoded, or quote an older formula after its exception changed. Neither
quotation supports a claim about the current executable expression.
The first optional executable-reference protocol, version 1, binds each selectable passage
to the complete request, candidate reading, exact question and representation. It pro-
vides separate references for the scope expression, result expression and complete rep-
resentation. That first design leaves a subtle problem: the representation also contains
freely written fact descriptions. A description containing a line headed Scope: can look
like the start of a second program expression to a text-matching routine. Accurately
quoting that description would still fail to identify the proposed program. Likewise, a
hash supplied alongside a representation cannot establish that the representation came
from the retained reading. Both can be changed together.
Version 2 therefore starts with the reading and question retained by the investigation,
independently of the request being checked. It parses the reading’s scope and result,
renders those two expressions using the existing controlled language, and locates their
program block after the fact descriptions. Only these expressions receive selectable
references. The entire representation remains visible so that fact meanings and qualifi-
cations are available for reasoning, but explanatory prose does not become executable
evidence merely by resembling a heading. The transmitted reading hash, question and
representation must match the retained originals before a model is called and again
when its response is resolved.
Each reference records its expression kind, the reading and question hashes, the for-
malization and representation hashes, and the exact Unicode character positions of the
quoted expression. The model selects the identifier; deterministic software retrieves
the original text. Changing the request, reading, question or expression invalidates the
old selections, even when a short expression looks identical. An expression owned by
another candidate cannot be borrowed. The parser and renderer remain software as-
sumptions in this transport check; the separate preservation proofs address their stated
formal boundaries.
Exact identity includes the type of each recorded value. An integer character offset
of zero and the Boolean value false are different JSON values, although Python’s or-
dinary equality treats them as equal. A reference-table check based on that equality
can accept altered metadata while returning the same quotation. The source and ver-
sion 2 executable resolvers therefore compare canonical serializations, which preserve
this distinction and reject floating-point offsets. The regression challenges these substi-
tutions before any text is selected. This check protects the evidence record; it adds no
support to the interpretation attached to that evidence.
An unencoded reading has no executable references. Its correspondence must remain
unassessed, or be declared inapplicable to the question with the separately required
justification. Software rejects a preserving, conflicting or omitting executable judgment

After references are resolved, the original source, question and correspondence checks
still apply. Exact quotation establishes what was discussed, not whether the discussion
is right.
The investigation uses source references while extracting claims, proposing readings
and defining questions.
It adds executable references at the later correspondence
stage, when both a particular reading and its question exist. This routing is part of the
recorded method. The resolver changes quotation identifiers into text; it preserves ev-
ery status, rationale, follow-up question and additional concern. The existing semantic
validator then checks source quotations, question identity and compatibility between
the proposed judgments. For example, an exact result quotation still cannot support a
preserving judgment when the same response says source support is unestablished.
A rejected response retains its original batch, perspective and reservation. The next
bounded attempt receives the diagnostic and prior-round evidence; the two perspec-
tives in one round receive the same earlier evidence. Failure at the attempt limit leaves
the required pairs unresolved. Version 1 records remain historical records rather than
being silently converted into successful version 2 observations. Replaying a response
under the new selection rules is possible only where its original quotation names an
available expression exactly. A longer prose quotation or a malformed paraphrase is
reported as unselectable, not replaced with evidence the model never supplied.
6.38.2 What a calendar comparison means
The retained UCITS readings use a date to delimit a proposed regulatory condition.
The legal selection of that date remains a separate question, but its mathematical com-
parison can be specified independently. We use valid dates in the proleptic Gregorian
calendar, from year 1 through year 9999. “Proleptic” means applying the same calen-
dar rule throughout this range, without reconstructing historical national changes of
calendar. The accepted spelling is the fixed-width form YYYY-MM-DD.
Let y, m and d be a valid year, month and day. A Gregorian leap year is divisible by four,
except for a year divisible by one hundred unless it is also divisible by four hundred.
Thus 1900 has 365 days and 2000 has 366. The number of days before the start of year y
is
Y (y) = 365(y −1) +

The first term counts ordinary days in preceding years. The remaining terms add four-
year leap days, remove century exceptions and restore four-hundred-year exceptions.
Let M(y, m) count the days in the completed months of year y; it is zero in January and
includes 29 February after February in a leap year. The zero-based ordinal of the date
is
O(y, m, d) = Y (y) + M(y, m) + d −1.
Consequently, 1 January in year 1 has ordinal zero. Moving to the next valid day in-
creases the ordinal by one, including across month and year boundaries.

The checked proposition equates strict comparison of these ordinals with lexicographic
comparison of valid year, month and day triples. The proof first checks that successive
year starts differ by the correct 365 or 366 days. Month lengths and starting offsets put
every valid day inside its year, with each month ending before the next begins. Dates
in different years are therefore ordered by their year starts; dates within one year are
ordered by their months and then days. The integer rank 372y + 31(m −1) + d has
the same order: it reserves 31 positions for each month and 372 for each year, enough
to prevent overlap between components. Those deliberately padded positions express
component ordering; they are not elapsed-day counts.
The independent formal-expression parser now accepts canonical date literals and date
facts in supported comparison expressions. It reconstructs the same constructor tree as
the shared model, and Lean checks that equality. The calendar theorem supplies a
declared meaning for date order; the constructor theorem checks preservation of the
expression using it. Neither theorem chooses the date intended by a legal provision.
Evidence timestamps, business-day calendars and date-arithmetic library functions re-
main separate.
The implementation also checks the representation boundary. Java compares canoni-
cal date strings, while the Catala adapter uses a day count relative to 1970. Subtracting
the same epoch from two ordinals preserves their comparison. An independent calen-
dar implementation is compared exhaustively with accepted canonical spellings and
the production Python date codec throughout the declared range. Native challenges
exercise equality, inclusive and strict comparison, leap days, century exceptions and
both endpoints through the actual RuleIR/Java and Catala routes. These are checks of
the codecs and selected runtime cases. The Lean theorem does not prove the Python
libraries, string comparator, Java compiler or Catala compiler.
6.38.3 Stronger formal evidence with legal questions retained
All eight encoded UCITS readings received constructor-preservation certificates. Their
sources, readings and questions are unchanged; the ninth remains unencoded. The
replay supplies no invented dates. Pending-application, incorporated-authority and
legal-date questions remain unresolved.
A later audit reproduced the three Gregorian propositions, all 3,652,059 valid dates
in the declared range and preservation evidence for the eight encoded readings. Its
49 known-date cases ran on each target, giving 98 native executions. Eight additional
requests with unknown or conflicting inputs abstained at the shared input boundary
before either target executed. These requests check the common boundary and can-
not count as independent native results. Their behavior also supplies no theorem for
arithmetic on unknown or conflicting dates.
Independent Boolean relations also check the HKMA calculations of Section 2.4.6 over
their full Boolean domains. Omitting each broker-exception condition produces a coun-
terexample. Both backends execute the proposals and abstain on incomplete or conflict-
ing input. The earlier eligibility increment passed 338 affected tests and completed 234

These results close specific software and mathematical gaps. Program agreement does
not establish legal correctness. Theorems cannot supply private bank mandates or ac-
count records. Future rules require new observations under a frozen method, before
further repairs. Development cases remain development evidence; future failures and
qualifications must be preserved.
